title: Troubleshoot Mobile Data - iOS
body:
# **Troubleshoot Mobile Data - iOS**

When mobile data stops working, apps and websites only load on Wi-Fi. Most of the time a setting or a stuck connection is to blame, and a few quick steps get it working again. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If the phone shows **SOS** or **No Service** at the top of the screen, this isn't a mobile data problem: use **Troubleshoot No Service** instead.

* * *

## 

**Check that mobile data is turned on**

Go to **Settings** > **Cellular** and make sure **Cellular Data** is turned on. On some phones this menu is called **Mobile Service** instead of **Cellular**; the switch is in the same place. If it's already on, move on to the next section.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer turn off Wi-Fi and open a website. An LTE or 5G icon coming back doesn't mean data works. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

# **Troubleshoot Messaging - iOS**

When text or picture messages won't send, they stay stuck with a red mark or a 'Not Delivered' note. Settings and network glitches are the usual causes. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If only messages to one person fail, the problem may be on their side; ask them to check their phone first.

* * *

## 

**Check the messaging settings**

Go to **Settings** > **Apps** > **Messages** and make sure **MMS Messaging** and **Send as Text Message** are on.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Software Update** and install anything available.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.

* * *

**Check the fix:** Have the customer send a test message to someone they know. A step can look like it worked before it really has.

If none of this helps, connect the customer with a specialist. Last reviewed 2026. Written for iOS 26. Related: Turn Airplane mode on or off, Reset network settings, Back up your phone.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If only messages to one person fail, the problem may be on their side; ask them to check their phone first.

* * *

## 

**Check the messaging settings**

Go to **Settings** > **Apps** > **Messages** and make sure **MMS Messaging** and **Send as Text Message** are on.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Update the software**

# **Troubleshoot Wi-Fi Connection Issues - iOS**

When a phone sees a Wi-Fi network but won't join it, a saved setting is often out of date. These steps refresh the connection. Work through the sections below in order, and check the fix after each one.

* * *

## 

**Before you start**

Find out what the customer already tried, so you don't repeat it. If no device in the home can connect, the router is the problem: use **Troubleshoot Home Internet** instead.

* * *

## 

**Forget the network and join it again**

Go to **Settings** > **Wi-Fi**, tap the info icon next to the network, tap **Forget This Network**, then join it again with the password.

* * *

## 

**Turn Airplane mode on and off**

Open **Control Center** by swiping down from the top-right corner, tap the airplane icon, wait 10 seconds, then tap it again. This makes the phone reconnect to the network.

* * *

## 

**Still not working?**

If the steps above didn't help, try these next, in this order.

**Restart the phone**

Press and hold the side button and either volume button until the slider appears, drag it, then turn the phone back on. Restarting clears minor glitches.

**Reset network settings**

Go to **Settings** > **General** > **Transfer or Reset iPhone** > **Reset** > **Reset Network Settings**. This clears saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and VPN settings, so get the customer's OK before they start.

On iPhone 8 and earlier, press and hold the top button instead of the side button to restart.
